title: Auth Control Plane authorization decision (v1 wire format)
description:
The decision point's answer to one authorization_request.v1 (TRD section 8, section 14).

THE FAIL-CLOSED RULE (TRD section 8: network, SDK, malformed-policy or PDP errors never return allow). `allowed` is REQUIRED, has NO default, and is a strict JSON boolean: a missing member, null, the string "true" or 1 is invalid, so a consumer can never read a malformed document as an allow. A consumer that cannot obtain a valid decision denies. A PDP failure is an error.v1 document (503), a different schema with a different `schema_version`, so "the decision point failed" and "the decision point said no" are distinguishable on the wire; this schema has no error member and cannot be mistaken for one.

BYTES, NOT OBJECTS. A JSON object may repeat a member and every parser keeps the last: `{"allowed":false,"allowed":true}` decodes to an allow. The schema validates the survivor and cannot see this. The clients therefore refuse duplicate members on the raw bytes before validating (see the reject_by_client fixtures).

`expires_at` is REQUIRED (lead ruling on Q2, CHAOS-4932: keep). TRD section 14's cache table makes decision expiry the bound on a stale allow, so a decision without one is invalid, deny as well as allow. `policy_revision` is required in every decision and is the ACP-ADR-05 monotonic revision of the active policy set (decision 3): every allow-cache key binds it. `reason_code` is a stable machine token, shape-only by reference to error.v1: user-facing text is caller-owned (TRD section 8), so free text is unrepresentable here.

schema_version.description: Identifies this document's contract. Reject an unrecognised value (G-26).

decision_id.description: Server-minted identifier correlating this decision with its audit row (TRD section 19). Never copied from caller input; fixed length as defence in depth, as in error.v1 request_id.

allowed.description: The decision. Required, no default, strict boolean. See the fail-closed rule above.

reason_code.description: Stable, safe-for-audit machine token naming why (e.g. allowed_by_repository_grant). Shape from error.v1 by reference; each surface owns and closes its own vocabulary.

principal_id.description: The principal the decision is about, from principal.v1.

organization_id.description: Organization the decision applies in, from principal.v1; null ONLY for a platform or pre-organization decision, never as a default.

policy_revision.description: ACP-ADR-05 policy revision the decision was made under; allow-cache keys bind it (G-31). Same definition as principal.v1; both clients accept only an integer token (a decimal or exponent form such as 42.0 is refused, CHAOS-4940) because the schema's `integer` admits it and cannot be the place it is caught.

expires_at.description: When this decision stops being usable (TRD section 14). Required for allow AND deny. After this instant the consumer must ask again; it must not reuse the decision.

tenant_scope.description: The organization every read and write for this decision must stay within. Enforced locally by the resource service (TRD section 8).

repository_allowlist.description: Canonical repository keys the service may touch; `*` means organization-wide. An empty array means NONE, not unrestricted: unrestricted is the absence of the member plus a tenant scope.

redaction.description: Field classes the service must remove from its response. Closed on purpose: an obligation the consumer does not recognise is worse than a deny, so an unknown redaction class makes the whole decision invalid and the consumer denies.

minimum_assurance.description: The authenticator assurance level the principal must hold for this decision to apply; a lower level means the service denies (G-29: ignoring an obligation is ignoring a denial).

step_up.description: True when the caller must complete step-up authentication before the action proceeds.

obligations.description: ENFORCEABLE obligations, not advice (TRD section 8: services enforce them locally). The member set is CLOSED and additionalProperties is false, so a decision carrying an obligation this contract does not define is invalid and fails closed rather than being half-honoured. Present only on an allow.

then.description: A deny carries no obligations: an obligation on a deny is meaningless and invites a consumer to act on it.
